result.topic_en: Euler resolves the Sun's or Moon's disturbing force on an Earth particle into a vertical component (changing gravity) and a horizontal component. He finds where gravity is increased or decreased (boundary at about 54°45') and the extreme values at the Earth's surface.
result.transcription:
258 INQUISITIO PHYSICA IN CAUSAM
fatis tutò fubftitui poterit $\frac{1}{a^3}+\frac{3x}{a^4}+\frac{3(4xx-yy)}{2a^5}$. Ex his autem obtinebitur vis, quâ particula $M$ præter gravitatem à vi Solis five Lunæ in $S$ exiftentis ad centrum Terræ $C$ in directione $MC$ urgetur, $=\frac{S(yy-2xx)}{a^3\sqrt{(x^2+y^2)}}+\frac{3Sx(3yy-2xx)}{2a^4\sqrt{(x^2+y^2)}}$.
Præterea autem eadem particula $M$ follicitabitur in directione $MR$ ad $MC$ normali, vi $=\frac{3Sxy}{a^3\sqrt{(x^2+y^2)}}+\frac{3Sy(4xx+yy)}{2a^4\sqrt{(x^2+y^2)}}$
$=\frac{3Sy}{a^3\sqrt{(x^2+y^2)}}\left(x+\frac{4xx-yy}{2a}\right)$. Atque cùm in his formulis termini primi pofteriores multis vicibus excedant, rem craffiùs infpiciendo, particula $M$ à vi Solis Lunæve fecundùm $MC$ urgebitur vi $=\frac{S(yy-2xx)}{a^3\sqrt{(x^2+y^2)}}$, in directione verò $MR$ vi $=\frac{3Sxy}{a^3\sqrt{(x^2+y^2)}}$.
§. 28. Ex his igitur poftremis formulis intelligitur ab actione Solis five Lunæ in $S$ exiftentis gravitatem particulæ $M$ augeri, fi ejus fitus refpectu rectæ $SC$ ita fuerit comparatus, ut fit $yy > 2xx$ hoc eft tangens anguli $MCP > \sqrt{2}$ pofito finu toto $= 1$, contrà verò gravitatem diminui, fi fuerit $yy < 2xx$. Quare cùm angulus cujus tangens eft $= \sqrt{2}$ contineat $54^\circ, 45'$ circiter, fi concipiatur circulus Terræ maximus quicunque $ADBE$, cujus planum per punctum $S$ tranfeat, in eoque ducantur rectæ $FCI$ & $GCH$, quæ cum rectâ $SAB$ angulos conftituant $54^\circ\ 45'$; tùm omnes Terræ particulæ in fpatiis $FCH$ & $GCI$ fitæ gravitatis naturalis augmentum accipient, reliquæ verò particulæ in fpatiis $FCG$ & $HCI$ pofitæ decrementum gravitatis patientur. Atque hinc, quâcunque Terræ particulâ propofitâ, definiri poterit, quantùm ejus gravitas à Sole Lunâve in $S$ exiftente vel augeatur vel diminuatur. Altera verò vis, quâ particula $M$ in directione horizontali $MR$ urgetur, affirmativa erit, in eamque plagam, quæ in figura repræfentatur, verget, fi quantitates $x$ & $y$ ambæ fuerint vel affirmativæ vel negativæ: contrariumque eveniet, fi earum altera fit affirmativa, altera negativa. Quare fi parti-
[margin: FIG. IV.; FIG. III.]

FLUXUS AC REFLUXUS MARIS. 259
cula $M$ fita fuerit vel in quadrante $ACD$ vel $ACE$, tum vis horizontalis ad rectam $CA$ tendet; contrà verò hæc vis ad radium $CB$ dirigetur, fi particula $M$ fit vel in quadrante $BCD$ vel $BCE$ conftituta. Ex quibus perfpicitur effectus vel Solis vel Lunæ in ambo hemifphæria, fuperius fcilicet $DAE$ & inferius $DBE$, inter fe effe ferè fimiles; quæ fimilitudo quoque in ipfo æftu Maris obfervatur.
§. 29. Ponamus nunc particulam $M$ in ipfâ Terræ fuperficie effe conftitutam, eritque $\sqrt{(x^2+y^2)} = 1$ ob Terræ femidiametrum $= 1$. Quare fi particula $M$ fuerit pofita in $M$, exiftente anguli $ACM$ finu $= y$ & cofinu $= x$, ejus gravitas naturalis acceleratrix à Sole Lunâve in $S$ augebitur vi $= \frac{S(yy-2xx)}{a^3}$, fecùndum horizontem autem in directione $MR$ urgebitur vi $= \frac{3Sxy}{a^3}$. Gravitas igitur maximè augebitur, fi particula $M$ pofita fuerit in $D$ vel $E$, quibus in locis punctum $S$ in horizonte apparet; ibi verò gravitatis augmentum erit $= \frac{S}{a^3}$. In punctis autem $A$ & $B$, quæ punctum $S$ vel in fuo zenith vel nadir pofitum habent, maximum deprehendetur gravitatis decrementum, quod fcilicet erit $= \frac{2S}{a^3}$; ita ut maximum gravitatis decrementum duplò majus fit quàm maximum incrementum. Vis autem horizontalis $\frac{3Sxy}{a^3}$ maxima evadet, fi angulus $ACM$ fuerit femirectus, id quod accidit in iis Terræ regionibus, in quibus punctum $S$ confpicitur vel $45^\circ$ gradibus fupra horizontem elevatum, vel tantundem fub horizonte depreffum latet: his igitur cafibus ob $xy = \frac{1}{2}$ fiet vis horizontalis $= \frac{3S}{2a^3}$. Hujus ergo vis effectus in hoc confiftet, ut directio gravitatis mutetur, atque versùs rectam $SC$ inclinetur angulo cujus tangens eft $= \frac{3S}{2a^3}$, exiftente finu toto $= 1$, quia gravitatem unitate defignamus.

items.quote: ita ut maximum gravitatis decrementum duplò majus fit quàm maximum incrementum
items.english: so that the greatest decrease of gravity is twice as large as the greatest increase.

items.quote: Ex quibus perfpicitur effectus vel Solis vel Lunæ in ambo hemifphæria, fuperius fcilicet $DAE$ & inferius $DBE$, inter fe effe ferè fimiles
items.english: From this it is seen that the effects of the Sun or the Moon on the two hemispheres, namely the upper DAE and the lower DBE, are nearly similar to each other.

items.quote: Atque hinc, quâcunque Terræ particulâ propofitâ, definiri poterit, quantùm ejus gravitas à Sole Lunâve in $S$ exiftente vel augeatur vel diminuatur.
items.english: Hence, for any given particle of the Earth, one can determine by how much its gravity is increased or diminished by the Sun or Moon placed at S.
